findings.shape: Two selected irregular rolled buff caps on shorter robust pale stipes bear dense downward teeth and partial tooth cues descending around the upper stipes. No woody bracket support is substituted for this terrestrial ectomycorrhizal fungus.
findings.surface: Muted apricot/buff numerical cap pigment, matte pale supports and geometric lower teeth distinguish it from translucent Pseudohydnum.
findings.movement: Stationary same bodies with an enlarged spore drift overlay. No locomotion, fruit-body growth, mycorrhizal physiology or measured airflow.
findings.evidenceScope: Actual D J Kelly public-domain photograph and selected Naturalis morphology compared. Primary Hydnum diversity/taxonomy text warns of overlapping macromorphology. The consulted Commons page leaves original geography unspecified, so the photograph is explicitly a source-labelled macro reference, not proof of a narrow molecular determination.
corrections: Reduced the three long-pillar first render to two shorter supported bodies.
Added denser underside/decurrent teeth, thinner rolled cap rims and warmer matte cap pigment.
findings.residual: Cap ripples and tooth placement are still regular, stipe/edge structure is simplified and proportions unmeasured. Original photo geography and narrow-species identification remain unresolved; microscopic traits, mycorrhizae and tissue optics are not simulated.

limits: Partly stylized, unmeasured original educational reconstructions. Fine anatomy, age variation, tissue optics, dimensions and physiology remain incomplete.
